_comment: Soft-coded configuration for the P&ID multi-pass analysis engine (PIDAnalysisService). Changes here take effect on next analysis run — no code deploy required.

pid_analysis._models_comment: Vision-capable models only. gpt-3.5 / gpt-4-base do NOT support images.
pid_analysis._pdf_comment: DPI used when rendering PDF pages to base64 images for the AI vision passes.
pid_analysis._ocr_comment: If embedded PDF text is shorter than ocr_sparse_threshold * 20 chars, Tesseract fallback is attempted.
pid_analysis._layout_comment: Layout detection pre-pass: a lightweight gpt-4o-mini call that identifies the drawing company standard, zone grid, title block position, and notes/legend positions BEFORE the main analysis passes. This context is injected into Passes 3, 5, and 6 so the AI can adapt to ANY P&ID layout style dynamically.
pid_analysis._thresholds_comment: QC thresholds. min_issues_target is injected into AI prompts as the minimum expected finding count for an IFC-stage drawing.
pid_analysis._pass3_comment: Pass 3: Main vision analysis (chain-of-thought, ISA-5.1, advanced compliance). Highest token budget — needs to return 20-50 structured findings.
pid_analysis._pass5_comment: Pass 5: Second review — broader zone-by-zone rescan for missed elements.
pid_analysis._pass6_comment: Pass 6: Engineering compliance deep-scan (PSV, valve standards, NACE, tie-ins, LTCS, etc.).
pid_analysis._pass7_comment: Pass 7: Line size validation & AI recommendation engine.
pid_analysis._pass8_comment: Pass 8: Smart QC enhancement (9 targeted checks: duplicates, valve sizing, notes/holds, TYPE designations, revision clouds, etc.).
pid_analysis._client_comment: OpenAI client-level timeout and retry settings.
pid_analysis._gemini_comment: Google Gemini provider. Set enabled=true and supply GEMINI_API_KEY env var to activate. Gemini 2.0 Flash supports 1M token context which yields richer, more complete reports. soft-coded: change models here without touching any Python code.
pid_analysis._routing_comment: Per-pass provider routing. Values: 'gemini' (Gemini first, OpenAI fallback) | 'openai' (OpenAI only). Changing a value here instantly re-routes that pass without any code change.
pid_analysis._cache_comment: S3 result cache. When enabled, the SHA-256 hash of the raw PDF bytes is used as a content-addressable key. Uploading the SAME file again (any filename, any user) immediately returns the stored report — all 8 AI passes are skipped. Set enabled=false to force a fresh analysis. ttl_days=0 means objects never expire automatically.
pid_analysis._hide_no_evidence_comment: When true, any finding returned to the report that has an empty or blank 'evidence' field is silently hidden from the engineer's view. This prevents undefended comments from reaching the P&ID review table. Set to false to show all findings regardless of evidence quality. No code deploy required — change this value and it takes effect on the next page load.
pid_analysis._suppress_comment: Categories to exclude from the final report. Any finding whose 'category' field (case-insensitive, partial match) appears in this list is silently dropped before the report is saved. Full category list: instrument, equipment, piping, valve, safety, control_loop, documentation, legend, pipe_class, psv_compliance, holds_compliance, notes_compliance, trim_class, dissimilar_material, ltcs_compliance, free_drain_slope, spool_requirement, critical_stress, valve_standard, tie_in_reference, corrosion_allowance. To re-enable a category, remove it from this list — no code deploy required.
pid_analysis._evidence_comment: Evidence writing standard injected into every AI pass system prompt. Controls how the AI justifies each finding. Edit here — no code deploy needed. The AI must follow this format for every 'evidence' field: VISUAL → GAP → STANDARD.

evidence_guidance.format_template: VISUAL: [describe exactly what is drawn — symbol present, tag readable, position on drawing, connections shown]. GAP: [state precisely what annotation, element, or connection is absent or non-compliant]. STANDARD: [cite the governing standard and clause, e.g. ISA-5.1 §6.4, API 520 Pt II §5.7.2, IEC 61511-1:2016 §11.6.5].
quality_rules: NEVER write 'not visible' without first stating exactly what IS visible and WHERE it is on the drawing.
NEVER cite a standard generically — name it explicitly (e.g. 'per applicable standard' is REJECTED; 'per ISA-5.1-2009 §6.4' is ACCEPTED).
NEVER reference a document not on the P&ID (datasheets, line lists, equipment schedules) as the location of the deficiency — the deficiency must be drawings observable.
If the element symbol IS visible but the annotation is missing, state: '[Tag] symbol is visible at [zone] on [line/equipment] — [annotation] is absent from the symbol/actuator.'
If the element itself is missing, state: 'No [element type] symbol is drawn on [specific line or nozzle] despite [equipment/standard] requiring one.'
For programmatic detections (OCR cross-checks, note references), state: 'Programmatically detected via OCR text extraction — visual confirmation by engineer recommended.'
Evidence must be specific enough that a different engineer reading it could locate the exact element on the drawing within 30 seconds.

instrument: ISA-5.1-2009 (Instrumentation Symbols and Identification) §6.4 — every transmitter must show a signal line to a receiver (DCS, controller, indicator)
IEC 61511-1:2016 (Functional Safety — SIS for Process Industry) §10 — SIL-rated instruments must show the SIS loop connection
ISA-TR84.00.02 (SIL Verification) — safety instrumented function requires sensor → logic solver → final element chain traceable on P&ID
AGES-GL-08-005 / ADNOC Instrument Standard — project-specific tag completeness and signal routing rules
valve: ISA-75.05.01 (Control Valve Terminology) — fail-safe position (FC/FO/FL) is a required annotation on every actuated valve symbol
IEC 61511-1:2016 §11.6.5 — all SIS final elements (SDV, BDV, XV) must show fail-safe mode on P&ID
API RP 14C:2017 (Offshore Safety Systems) — BDV must be annotated fail-open (FO) on the P&ID
API 6D:2021 (Pipeline and Piping Valves) — valve tag identification and pressure class marking on P&ID
ASME B16.34:2017 (Valves — Flanged, Threaded, Welding End) — pressure class designation required on P&ID valve annotation
piping: ISO 10628-2:2012 (P&ID Diagram Symbols) — line number format: Diameter-FluidCode-Sequence-PipeClass (e.g. 4"-HC-1001-CS150)
ASME B31.3:2022 (Process Piping) — pipe class applicability defines material, pressure rating, temperature range
AGES-SP-08-002 (Company Piping Material Class Specification) — spec break symbol and both upstream/downstream classes must be shown at every pipe class change
ISO 10628-1:2014 §6 — vent and drain connection requirements on vessels and pump casings
psv_compliance: API 520 Part II:2015 §5.7.2 — inlet block valve must be car-sealed open (CSO) on the P&ID; absence of CSO valve is a P&ID deficiency
API 521:2014 §5.15 — PSV discharge routed to flare header, vent stack, or labeled closed drain system must be shown on P&ID
ASME Section VIII Div 1 UG-135 — every pressure vessel requires a pressure relief device shown on the P&ID
API 520 Part I:2020 — set pressure, relieving capacity, back pressure are DATASHEET items NOT required on P&ID
equipment: API 610:2021 (Centrifugal Pumps for Petroleum) §7.3.1 — suction strainer (Y-type or basket) must be shown on suction side of all process pumps
API 610:2021 §9.3 — check valve on pump discharge line required to prevent backflow; must appear on P&ID
API 650:2021 (Welded Tanks for Oil Storage) — vent nozzle, drain, and level instrument connections must be shown
ASME Section VIII Div 1 — vessel design conditions (P/T) in data box on P&ID when included in IFC package
API 661:2006 (Air-Cooled Heat Exchangers) — block and isolation valves on inlet/outlet headers shown on P&ID
control_loop: ISA-5.1-2009 §6 — every PID controller (FIC, PIC, TIC, LIC) requires a visible, tagged final control element (FCV, PCV, TCV) on the same process loop on the P&ID
ISA-5.4-1991 (Instrument Loop Diagrams) — signal line must be traceable from sensor through controller to final element
IEC 61511-1:2016 §10 — SIS loop completeness: sensor → logic solver → final element chain must be traceable on P&ID
documentation: ISO 10628-1:2014 §7.4 — every symbol used in the drawing body must be defined in the drawing legend; undefined symbols are legend integrity failures
ISO 10628-1:2014 §7.6 — elements inside a revision cloud must cross-reference the revision table with a revision code and date
IFC Review Checklist (EPC standard) — all HOLD items must show a resolution status, responsible engineer, or target date
ASME Y14.5 / ISO 1101 — tag identification completeness and drawing number format
safety: IEC 61511-1:2016 §11.6 — SIS field devices (PSHH, LSHH, TSHH) must show their SIS/ESD signal line connection on P&ID
API RP 505:1994 (Fire and Gas Detection) — F&G detector positions shown on P&ID and layout must be consistent
AGES-SP-17-001 (ESD Philosophy) — ESD valve numbering convention and SIS signal lines must be on P&ID

examples.good_evidence: VISUAL: BDV-2101 actuated valve symbol with a solenoid (XY) actuator is clearly drawn in the Middle-Right zone on the 6"-BD-2101-CS300 blowdown header. The SIS signal line from XY is present. GAP: No fail-safe position annotation (FO, FC, or FL) is shown adjacent to the actuator symbol; the standard position next to the actuator body is blank. STANDARD: ISA-75.05.01 requires fail-safe position on every actuated valve; IEC 61511-1:2016 §11.6.5 mandates it for all SIS final elements; API RP 14C:2017 specifically requires FO (fail-open) annotation for blowdown valves in hydrocarbon gas service.

VISUAL: PT-3105 pressure transmitter circle-bubble is visible in the Top-Right zone, connected to the 3"-HC-3105-CS150 suction header tapping. The transmitter symbol itself is correctly drawn with a readable tag. GAP: No signal line (dashed or solid) extends from PT-3105 to any DCS node, indicator, or controller; the output side of the bubble terminates without a connection. STANDARD: ISA-5.1-2009 §6.4 requires every transmitter to show a signal line to a receiving element. An unconnected transmitter cannot perform its measurement function and will not be wired during construction.

VISUAL: PSV-1015 relief valve symbol is drawn at the top nozzle of Vessel V-1015 in the Middle-Left zone with a readable tag. The inlet pipe connects directly from the vessel nozzle to the PSV inlet. GAP: No flanged gate valve with a car-sealed open (CSO) annotation is drawn between the vessel nozzle and PSV-1015; the connection is a direct stub without any isolation valve. STANDARD: API 520 Part II:2015 §5.7.2 requires a CSO block valve on every PSV inlet to enable maintenance isolation without depressurising the vessel. Absence on the P&ID means it will not be installed during construction.

VISUAL: A 6-inch horizontal process line is visible across the Bottom-Center zone between Pump P-2201A discharge nozzle and the shell-side inlet of Heat Exchanger E-2201. The line carries the annotation '6"-HC-2201'. GAP: The pipe specification/class designator (e.g. CS150, SS300, A1A) is absent from the line number; only the size (6"), fluid code (HC), and sequence (2201) are shown. STANDARD: ISO 10628-2:2012 line number format requires SIZE-FluidCode-Sequence-PipeClass. Without the class designator, construction teams cannot select compliant flanges, fittings, bolting, and gaskets per ASME B31.3:2022 Table A-1.

VISUAL: Centrifugal pump P-3601A symbol is visible in the Bottom-Left zone. A gate valve and straight pipe run are drawn on the suction side between Vessel V-3601 bottom outlet and the pump suction nozzle. GAP: No strainer symbol (Y-type or basket) is drawn on the suction pipe between the isolation valve and P-3601A suction nozzle — the suction run is a plain pipe with only a gate valve. STANDARD: API 610:2021 §7.3.1 requires a suction strainer on all centrifugal pumps in hydrocarbon service to protect impeller and mechanical seal from solid particles. Absence on the IFC P&ID means it will not be installed, risking pump damage at commissioning startup.

VISUAL: FIC-4201 flow indicating controller bubble is visible in the Top-Center zone with a dashed signal line from FT-4201 transmitter on the 4"-HC-4201-CS150 line. The controller bubble is complete with tag. GAP: No control valve (FCV-4201 or tagged equivalent) is shown anywhere on the 4"-HC-4201-CS150 line downstream — the process line runs from FT-4201 to the downstream vessel without any final control element in the loop. STANDARD: ISA-5.1-2009 §6 requires every PID controller to have a visible, tagged final control element as part of the same control loop on the P&ID. An incomplete control loop at IFC stage means the valve will be missing from the construction bill of materials.
